name: Space Explorer
description: Travel the solar system and discover alien creatures on every planet!

reward.name: Solar Salamander
reward.fact: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and a year there lasts just 88 Earth days.

reward.name: Cloud Serpent
reward.fact: Venus spins backwards compared to most planets — the Sun rises in the west there!

reward.name: Dust Devil Fox
reward.fact: Mars has the tallest volcano in the solar system — Olympus Mons is three times higher than Everest.

reward.name: Storm Whale
reward.fact: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm that has been raging for over 350 years and is bigger than Earth.

reward.name: Ring Glider
reward.fact: Saturn's rings are made of billions of chunks of ice and rock, some as small as grains of sand.

reward.name: Ice Crystal Moth
reward.fact: Uranus rolls around the Sun on its side — scientists think a massive collision knocked it over billions of years ago.

reward.name: Deep Space Octopus
reward.fact: Neptune has the strongest winds in the solar system, blowing at over 1,200 miles per hour.

reward.name: Lunar Rabbit
reward.fact: The Moon has no atmosphere, so footprints left by astronauts in 1969 are still there today.

reward.name: Asteroid Beetle
reward.fact: There are millions of asteroids in our solar system, but if you put them all together they'd still be smaller than our Moon!

reward.name: Nebula Jellyfish
reward.fact: Nebulae are giant clouds of dust and gas where new stars are born. Some are over 100 light-years across!

reward.name: Comet Fox
reward.fact: Halley's Comet visits Earth every 75-76 years. It was last seen in 1986 and will return in 2061!

reward.name: Twin Star Wolves
reward.fact: More than half of all star systems have two or more stars orbiting each other — our single Sun is actually unusual!

reward.name: Station Cat
reward.fact: The International Space Station orbits Earth 16 times a day, meaning astronauts see 16 sunrises every 24 hours!

reward.name: Void Raven
reward.fact: A black hole's gravity is so strong that not even light can escape. Time itself slows down near one!

reward.name: Ice Penguin
reward.fact: Pluto is so far from the Sun that it takes 248 Earth years to complete one orbit — one Pluto year!

reward.name: Methane Frog
reward.fact: Saturn's moon Titan has lakes and rivers, but they're made of liquid methane instead of water!

reward.name: Ice Dolphin
reward.fact: Jupiter's moon Europa has a hidden ocean under its icy surface that may contain more water than all of Earth's oceans!

reward.name: Colony Hamster
reward.fact: A day on Mars is only 37 minutes longer than a day on Earth — so your bedtime would barely change!

reward.name: Lava Gecko
reward.fact: Jupiter's moon Io has over 400 active volcanoes — it's the most volcanic place in the entire solar system!

reward.name: Shadow Panther
reward.fact: Ganymede is the largest moon in our solar system — it's even bigger than the planet Mercury!

reward.name: Nova Phoenix
reward.fact: When a massive star explodes as a supernova, it briefly shines brighter than an entire galaxy of billions of stars!

reward.name: Warp Chameleon
reward.fact: Scientists think wormholes could be shortcuts through space-time, connecting two distant parts of the universe!

reward.name: Shadow Owl
reward.fact: About 85% of all matter in the universe is dark matter — it's invisible and scientists still don't know what it's made of!

reward.name: Alien Axolotl
reward.fact: Scientists have discovered over 5,000 planets outside our solar system — some might have conditions for life!

reward.name: Galaxy Bear
reward.fact: Our Milky Way galaxy contains between 100 and 400 billion stars — and the Sun is just one of them!

reward.name: Commander Eagle
reward.fact: It takes radio signals about 13 minutes to travel from Mars to Earth — so Mars rovers have to think for themselves!

reward.name: Signal Bat
reward.fact: There are over 7,000 satellites orbiting Earth right now. The furthest human-made object, Voyager 1, is over 24 billion kilometres away!

reward.name: Navigator Hawk
reward.fact: Ancient sailors used the stars to navigate. The North Star barely moves in the sky, so it always shows which way is north!

reward.name: Fuel Cell Beetle
reward.fact: The Space Shuttle needed 2 million litres of fuel just to launch — that's enough to fill 30 swimming pools!

reward.name: Stardust Firefly
reward.fact: Every atom in your body was once inside a star that exploded. You are literally made of stardust!

reward.name: Plasma Butterfly
reward.fact: The solar wind is a stream of particles blasting from the Sun at 1.6 million kilometres per hour. Earth's magnetic field protects us from it!

reward.name: Voyager Whale
reward.fact: The Voyager Golden Record carries sounds and images from Earth into deep space — including whale songs, music, and greetings in 55 languages!
